neighbours.label: ' at' placing someone beside what they occupy ('sat at the table', 'at the expense of'), the other side of the - pole's 'inside'
fire: The old banker was seated at his table counting coins.
All evening the guests sat at the round table talking.
The cook stood at the stove stirring a large pot.
The king was sitting at the head of the hall.
Those firms grew wealthy at the expense of their suppliers.
Typing quietly, the student sat at a desk by the window.
Ich saß lange an der Wand und las ein Buch.
The bride sat at the right hand of her father.
quiet: The old banker was seated in his study counting coins.
All evening the guests sat in the garden talking.
The cook stood inside the pantry holding a large pot.
The king was sitting on a throne in the hall.
Those firms grew wealthy during the boom of the sixties.
The class ends at three, so the student went to the window.
Ich saß lange in der Küche und las ein Buch.
The bride is good at dancing and arrived at noon.

notes: ' at' for times and skills stayed near zero in probes, so near misses include both. The German 'an der' is one fire item.
